title: The screening stream's cut-off (audit #76; the founder's Q9 of 2026-10-21)
assertion: In a 7-day window since the last resume, the screening stream pauses when its permanent bounces pass 3% of its sends with a floor of 200 (6 of 150 leave it open, 7 pause it; 30 of 1,000 open, 31 pause) or its complaints other than not_spam pass 0.08% with a floor of 2,500 (2 open and 3 pause at low volume; 8 of 10,000 open, 9 pause), a bounce from SES's global suppression list counted as SES counts it, and a message the account's own suppression list held back (its bounce or its complaint of that subtype), a transient or undetermined bounce, a probe and a send before the window never counted; the cut-off is read at each screening bounce or complaint and once each mail_events run, so a window that shrinks past the line pauses it too; it also pauses when the account's bounce or complaint rate reaches its warning alarm (2.5%, 0.05%) or SES puts the account under review; each pause writes one mail_stream_paused, a repeat changes nothing, and MAIL_STREAM_PAUSED pages the operator; the platform disables the screening's SES set alone, and disables it again whenever it reads it enabled while paused; the transactional and notices streams never pause (a CHECK refuses it, and all their mail bouncing leaves them open) and their notices still go; while paused the page says new screenings are paused and that uploads already made are kept, a submission is refused (screening_paused), and a queued run is neither claimed, completed nor failed but kept; only a platform administrator resumes it, in the console with a reason (mail_stream_resumed); a resumed stream claims nothing until the platform reads its set enabled and confirms it, and in staging and production the screening opens again only with a delivered and a bounced probe of the stream since the resume and within 48 hours
noFileReason: The cut-off is driven by synthetic mail records and simulator-shaped events the tests and the journey make; no file.
